subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about mangrove forests?

options.text: Mangrove forests stabilise the coastline, reducing erosion.
Mangrove trees grow in areas with oxygen-rich soil.

solution:
The correct answer is__** Mangrove trees grow in area with oxygen rich soil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mangrove Forest**

 
 
• **Mangrove forests** are **fertile wetlands** that grow in coastal intertidal zones.
 
• They are also known as **mangrove swamps, mangrove thickets, or mangals**.
 
• By **stabilising the coastline**, mangrove forests help to **prevent erosion** brought on by storm surges, currents, waves, and tides.
 
• Mangroves are **salt tolerant herbs**.
 
• Mangrove trees come in roughly **80 different species**. All of these trees thrive in **low-oxygen soil environments** with slowly moving rivers that allow fine sediments to build up. 
 
• Because mangrove **trees cannot tolerate freezing temperatures**, mangrove forests only occur at tropical and subtropical latitudes. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Many mangrove forests can be identified by the** tangled mass of prop roots** that give the trees the appearance of being elevated above the water.
 
• The **majority of mangroves experience flooding at least twice daily because of the trees' ability to cope with the daily rise and fall of the tides **due to their complex web of roots.
 
• **Fish and other species seeking food and safety **from predators find these woods to be attractive because of the intricate root systems of mangroves.
 
• Mangrove forests serve as c**enters for the movement of matter and energy** between these systems because they are situated where **the land, ocean, and atmosphere converge**. 
 
• These mangrove ecosystems' most important components are **marine microorganisms**.
